sections.text: While he whose purpose is infirm, who is low-minded, stubborn, dishonest, malicious, indolent, despondent, procrastinating - he may be assumed to be in Darkness.
Reason and conviction are threefold, according to the Quality which is dominant. I will explain them fully and severally, O Arjuna!
प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये।

That intellect which understands the creation and dissolution of life, what actions should be done and what not, which discriminates between fear and fearlessness, bondage and deliverance, that is Pure.

So we had been discussing chapter 18, Moksha Sannyasa Yoga. Just to remind ourselves what we have seen so far: in the beginning, Arjuna made a request -- I want to know what is Sannyasa and what is Tyaga? Because we had been talking about renunciation. This chapter is called Liberation through Renunciation.
So the obvious answer is renouncing actions. And how do we renounce actions and what type of actions can we renounce or should we renounce is the gist of this chapter. So the first thing Bhagavan said is Kamyanam Karmanam Nyasa Iti Sannyasa -- giving up all the desire-prompted actions is Sannyasa.
Thats as simple as it is. If I can give up all desire prompted actions so that Im truly driven by my duties, the joy of working and whatever is appropriate for me to work, then I am a sannyasi. But that may or may not be possible.
So the next is Sarvakarma Falat Tyaga Iti Tyaga. If you give up all the Karma Phala, the desire for the fruits of action, then its Tyaga. So Bhagavan starts with Tyaga because that may be more appropriate for us.
So then he describes that even tyaga can be of three different types. So now the entire chapter takes up the aspect of actions -- which is what is binding us. Actions in our day-to-day life, what we call work, are becoming a burden for us.
Thats why we all want to retire. All our planning for is what retirement. Thats because we are not enjoying the work.
So Bhagawan said lets understand what tyaga is. So then we have seen that the tyaga also can be of three types of you can give up something which is youre appropriately giving up because of sattvic reasons or rajasic reasons or tamasic reasons. Then we said the tyaga we talked about of actions.
So what type of actions should be given up and what should not be given up? We said the yajna dana tapa, this type of actions must be performed. So even the yajnas can be of three types. Sattvik, Rajasika, Tamasik, Dana also can be of three types.
SattVik, Rajasik and tamasic. The disciplines which we follow can also be three types. Sattvik, rajasik, tamasik.
In other words, everything is tied to each other. How we think, how we behave and what the results come to us, theyre all tied to each other. Our thinking is not sattvic, then obviously our actions will not be sattvic and therefore our results will not be satwik.
So if we understand this mechanism of actions, then maybe we will be able to liberate ourselves from this burden of work. In India, at least in the 60s that I can remember, the first thing people would ask is, So where are you working? Oh, I just got a job in government. I think its a perfect job.
Ill tell you, I hardly have to work. The definition of good job in many times in India was the job in which I did the least amount of work is a good job. Now is it really what Im looking for in a job? I remember when I went to Zambia.
I took a job at the building department in the government of Zambia. So my chief architect, first day in orientation said, we have a requirement that in a year you should at least do three drawings. And I said, are you serious? He said, no, at least you should have three drawings in a year.
So that was a government standard of your performance. Our basic understanding right now is that action is a burden. Actually, as long as I can get out of the actions, then Ill be happy.
So renouncing action is the goal of our life. But how to renounce action is the theme of this chapter. So we say even yajna dana tapas, which needs to be done also should be done in a manner that it liberates you and not binds you.
So yagnas can be of three types, Dhyana can be of three types, and tapas can be of three types. And we all know sometimes we do charity. But that makes you unhappy.
Instead of making you feel joy about giving, it makes you unhappy. Thats because our attitude towards giving had something not right about it. So Bhagavan said, you should examine this thing in all things you do, whether its sattvik, tamasic or rajasik, and see what is appropriate for you.
Then we said, okay, Karma. Now lets understand what is the nature of Karma. And I said: Karma, Karana, Karta.
These are the three constituent parts of any action. Any action will have an action, a doer, and an instrument of action. And that requires knowledge.
Gnanam, Gneyam, Parignata -- these are the three constituent parts: the knowledge, that which is to be known, and the knower. If we understand the mechanism of these actions and how the knowledge takes place, then we should be able to work better. So then we have looked at how the knowledge takes place and how the action is related to it.
So then we have been looking at and say, okay, now if knowledge also can be of three types. Some knowledge is Sattvic, some is Rajasic and some is Tamasic. Something I come to believe without any reason or rhyme could be tamasic.
So knowledge also can be Sattvik, Rajasik or Tamasik. I should be very careful. Even I consider myself a more knowledgeable person.
I need to examine whether my knowledge is appropriate or Sattvik or Rajasik or Tamasakya. Obviously, before whoever figured it out that earth is round, people had knowledge the earth is flat. But it was not really a knowledge based on any basis, but just a regular observation that looks like earth is flat.
So sometimes what is quite obvious may not be the truth. So I need to be constantly vigilant about it. So my knowledge also should be examined whether it is Rajasik, Tamasik or Sattvik.
Then Karma, which I am performing, also can be Rajasic, Tamasic or Sattvik, depending on the knowledge which I have, is whether Sattvik, Rajasik or Tamasik. So these are all tied together in every aspect of my life. I should be examining whether this is the most appropriate way to behave.
So then the verses which well be saying today they about Karta, Karta. I consider myself the doer. Now am I a Sattvik doer, a Rajasic doer, a Tamasic doer? Then we find out that its not a consistent that I am not always a Sattvic doer, Im not always a Rajasik doer.
Im not always a Tamasik doer. At times Im Sattvik, at times Im Rajasik, at times Im Tamasik. However, I must examine that and make sure that I do not become predominantly Tamasic or Rajasic.
Because the results of Tamas and Rajas, as we have seen, are nothing but pain in the end. The only thing which liberates you is sattva, the pure knowledge. When I start seeing things as they are, thats where the liberation comes in.
Anytime I have bias of my own, then Im bound by my own bias. More and more people realizing that more they limit themselves to one viewpoint or one group of people, theyre binding themselves to limitations. The more they open up, they become more liberated and make more progress.
So the verse 26 says Mukta Sangha Anahamvadi Dhruti Utsa Samanvitah Siddhi Asidyo nirvikaraha karta satvika uchate. If I am a doer and I consider myself the person performing this action, well, lets see in what attitude I perform it. Mukta Sangha -- free from attachment.
Am I really too attached to this action? If somebody lets me do it, great. If I dont get a chance to do this, am I okay? Or is the world going to come apart if I dont get a chance to do this? Unattached. Anahamvadi -- he does not have the ego that I am the doer. I am the only one who can do it.
I can do this so that we know that if I can do it, the others can also do it. However, I can put the best efforts if I want. Dhruti Utsa Samanvitah -- I think this, at least from my life, is the most important part.
Whether you are successful or not successful in what you are pursuing. Again dhruti persistent firmness. This is what I want to do.
When I came to this country, I kept giving my lifes example because thats all I know is my life. When I came to this country, I met some architects who had been here 10 years before I had come. So I asked their advice and said what should I do? I need to get registration as a licensed architect in this country.
They forget about it. Its not really worth it. It will take you 10 years.
There are better professions with your architectural training. You can be a pipe draftsman or something which will give you a better compensation. And I say, Ill tell you honestly, the only thing I know is architecture.
So I need to pursue architecture. Whether there are good chances in this country or not. I have to continue find my niche because I dont know anything better.
But I say only thing I know is doing architecture. So Dhruti -- if you want to be successful in architecture, stay with architecture. Dont buy a gas station; dont open up a hotel.
Dhruti is the most important aspect of any actions we will perform. If you are yourself not firm about it, people will recognize right away that you are not serious about it. And the next quality is Utsaha -- enthusiasm.
There was a unique quality: he would infuse enthusiasm in anybody he met. Everybody in front of him was like we can do this and we can do that. Thats a unique quality that you can inspire people to be enthusiastic about what they are doing.
And again, if you are not enthusiastic, everybody else will be also the same way. The most important aspects of any doer are Dhruti and Utsaha -- Samanvitah Siddhi Asidyo Nirvikaraha. Having done all that, the result is not in my hand.
I may be the best person, I may be the best firm. But the world may have different needs and the world may react differently. And therefore it may not be a successful action.
And I should be unattached to that. Do not get affected by it. We are human beings, we have emotions.
We may feel slightly bad about it, but you have to move on from that. It should not affect your personality that now Im rejected one time, I will not try next time. In fact, continue trying to persistently keep going back and back to the same organization or efforts to be successful.
Persistence pays off. Siddhi Asidyo Nirvikarah karta satvikochate. Such an actor, such a doer is considered Sattvik.
He may be successful, he may not be successful. He may be appreciated. He may not be appreciated.
But he knows that hes pursuing this with all his zeal and all firmness. So thats such a doer is Sattvik the next one. Ragi Karma Phala prepsuhu lubdaha in Satmakaha Asuchi Harshoka Anvitah karta Rajasah Parikertita.
However, when we are in that mode, we dont recognize it. Unfortunately, its a ragi attached sometimes with a good virtue. Hes very passionate about it. Passion is something which can be very tricky to recognize whether it is positive or negative.
The same passion, it is based on your dhruti then it is positive.

Verse 28 completes the portrait of the tamasic doer: ayukta (undisciplined), prakrita (vulgar), stabdha (obstinate), shatha (deceitful), naishkritika (malicious), alasa (lazy), vishadi (despondent), and dirgha-sutri (procrastinating). This is a catalog of self-defeating tendencies that prevent meaningful action. The combination is revealing - laziness paired with obstinacy, deceit with procrastination. These qualities feed on each other, creating a downward spiral that keeps one trapped in inertia and ineffectiveness.
Verses 29-30 shift to buddhi (intellect), the guiding faculty that determines which actions to pursue. Sattvic buddhi knows pravritti (what should be done) and nivritti (what should be avoided), karya (duty) and akarya (non-duty), bhaya (what to fear) and abhaya (what not to fear), bandha (bondage) and moksha (liberation). This discriminative capacity is the cornerstone of wise living. Without clear buddhi, even good intentions lead to confused actions. The sattvic intellect serves as an internal compass, consistently pointing toward what truly matters.
Examine your own buddhi today: How clear is your discrimination between what binds you and what liberates you? We often know intellectually what we should do but find ourselves doing the opposite. This gap indicates the need to strengthen sattvic buddhi through consistent practice. Ask yourself: In the decisions I face today, can I clearly see which choice leads toward freedom and which toward bondage? Make one choice today based purely on this discrimination - not on what feels good or what others expect, but on what your purified intellect recognizes as the path to liberation.
